title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I)
keywords_en: marriage; handling cases related to the Wenchuan earthquake
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on the Application of Law in Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I)

Fa Fa [2008] No. 21

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to properly handle trial and enforcement work in the disaster-stricken areas and protect the lawful rights and interests of the people in those areas, the Supreme People's Court has formulated the Opinions on the Application of Law in Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I), which are hereby issued to you for implementation in accordance with trial practice.

All High People's Courts, especially those in areas severely affected by the disaster, shall strengthen their research on the trial and enforcement of relevant cases, and report any new situations or issues to the Supreme People's Court in a timely manner.

July 14, 2008

Supreme People's Court

Opinions on the Application of Law in Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I)

In order to properly handle trial and enforcement work in the disaster-stricken areas, protect the lawful rights and interests of the people in those areas, maintain social stability in the disaster-stricken areas, and provide strong judicial guarantees for earthquake relief and post-disaster recovery and reconstruction, the Supreme People's Court issued the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Properly Handling Trial Work during Earthquake Relief and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in Disaster-Stricken Areas (Fa [2008] No. 152) on May 27, 2008, and the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Properly Handling Civil Trial and Enforcement Work during Earthquake Relief, Recovery and Reconstruction (Fa [2008] No. 164) on June 6, 2008. The above two Notices set forth the basic principles for the trial and enforcement of disaster-related cases and some specific issues concerning the application of law, which shall be strictly implemented by people's courts at all levels. In light of the actual situation of post-disaster recovery and reconstruction, and in order to restore the normal economic and social order in the disaster-stricken areas as soon as possible, the following opinions are hereby further put forward on issues concerning the application of law in cases related to the Wenchuan earthquake disaster:

1. For cases involving personal and property relations of people in the disaster-stricken areas, such as marriage and family, inheritance, declaration of death, and declaration of disappearance, the people's courts shall actively accept them in accordance with the law and promptly resolve issues arising from changes in personal and property rights and obligations caused by the earthquake.

2. If the resettlement place of people in the disaster-stricken areas is not in the same administrative region as their original domicile or habitual residence, for lawsuits filed after resettlement in a different place, the resettlement place may be deemed as the party's domicile for the purpose of determining jurisdiction in accordance with the law.

3. If contracted rural land becomes uncultivable or its boundaries become unclear due to the earthquake disaster, and the parties file a lawsuit requesting adjustment, boundary demarcation, or re-identification of rights, the people's court shall inform the parties to apply to the relevant government administrative department for resolution.

4. If the judge presiding over a case is unable to perform his or her duties due to death or other reasons, the people's court may replace the case handler to continue the trial in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Collegial Panels in People's Courts (Fa Shi [2002] No. 25). If a case is transferred or placed under designated jurisdiction, the people's court receiving the transfer or designated jurisdiction shall continue the trial.

5. In criminal cases, civil cases, administrative cases, or enforcement cases that are being tried by the people's court, if a party dies or disappears, the matter shall be handled separately in accordance with the law. If the defendant in a criminal case dies, the trial shall be terminated. If a party in a civil case, administrative case, or enforcement case dies or disappears, a ruling shall be made to suspend the trial or enforcement. After the resettlement and recovery and reconstruction work in the disaster-stricken area has progressed to a certain stage, and after the personal and property relations involved in the case have been clarified through legal procedures, the people's court shall decide in accordance with the law whether to resume the trial or enforcement, or to treat the case as withdrawn, terminate the litigation, terminate the enforcement, or change the subject of the case, etc.

6. If evidence submitted by a party to the court in litigation consists of originals that are lost in the earthquake before being cross-examined, and the facts to be proved or the content of the lost or destroyed evidence cannot be proved by other means, the people's court shall properly handle the matter through mediation or other methods.

7. With regard to the determination of the date when "the cause for the suspension of the limitation period is eliminated" as provided in Article 139 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the date when "the impediment is removed" as provided in Article 76 of the Civil Procedure Law, the date when "the cause for the suspension of the lawsuit is eliminated" as provided in Article 136 of the Civil Procedure Law, the date when "the circumstances for suspension disappear" as provided in Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law, and the date when "the cause for the suspension of the lawsuit is eliminated" as provided in Article 51 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the principle of lenient application shall be adhered to, taking into account the different circumstances in the disaster-stricken areas and the specific conditions of each individual case.

When making such determinations, the people's court may consider the following factors: (1) the status of the court's return to normal work; (2) the progress of local recovery and reconstruction; (3) the reappearance of a missing party, the appointment of a property custodian in accordance with the law, or the determination of death by the relevant authorities or the declaration of death by the people's court, thereby clarifying the heirs; (4) the restoration of business capacity of a party that is a legal person or other organization, or the determination of a successor to rights and obligations.

8. If a party to a case being tried goes missing in the earthquake disaster, the people's court may serve legal documents by public announcement after verifying the party's identity and whereabouts.

If an interested party applies for a declaration of disappearance of a missing person, after the people's court renders a judgment declaring the person missing, the property custodian shall be changed to the party, and the relevant legal documents shall be served on the property custodian.

9. If property that has been sealed, distrained, or frozen is damaged or lost due to the earthquake during litigation, the matter shall be handled by reference to Article 24 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Sealing, Distraint, and Freezing of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts; if the applicant provides other property leads and applies for sealing or distraint, the application fee may be waived.

For property that has already been appraised but is damaged or depreciated in value due to the earthquake, a new appraisal may be conducted upon the applicant's request, and the appraisal fee shall be determined in accordance with Article 12 of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Fees.

10. If the enforcement applicant is an enterprise or citizen not located in the disaster-stricken area, and the enforcement respondent is an enterprise or citizen in the disaster-stricken area, and the property cannot be identified or there is no property available for enforcement, enforcement shall be suspended; if the enforcement respondent has property available for enforcement after suffering the disaster, the enforcement agency shall endeavor to facilitate a settlement to conclude the case; if the enforcement applicant requests continued enforcement, but enforcement of such property would seriously affect the smooth progress of recovery and reconstruction, enforcement may be suspended. After the circumstances leading to the suspension of enforcement disappear, enforcement shall be resumed in a timely manner.

If a disaster-stricken enterprise or citizen applies for compulsory enforcement, and the enforcement respondent is an enterprise or citizen not located in the disaster-stricken area, the people's court shall strengthen enforcement efforts and enforce promptly in accordance with the law, so as to facilitate the better recovery of production and reconstruction of homes for the disaster-stricken enterprises and citizens.
